bea4403e-c18d-4922-903e-ba738acd5878.name: Accommodation
bea4403e-c18d-4922-903e-ba738acd5878.value:
On-campus Housing
UNSW affiliated Colleges and Apartments provide high quality accommodation and you should apply directly to the College or Apartment as early as possible. On campus accommodation is extremely limited and is not guaranteed even if you apply by the deadline. 

Off-campus Housing
Most exchange students choose to live off campus and enjoy the beautiful suburbs that surround UNSW. Sydney is a safe city, with public transport connecting the UNSW campuses, beaches, and city centre. We recommend students arrive 1-2 weeks early to find off campus accommodation. You may wish to book temporary accommodation to allow time to find more permanent housing.
* Off campus support offered by UNSW accommodation team https://www.unsw.edu.au/student/student-life/campus/accommodation

1. Student Visa Conditions: All international students in our Study Abroad and Exchange programs
are required to have a valid student visa. See this page for details regarding Student Visa
(Subclass 500) conditions. https://students.mq.edu.au/support/international/student-visa
2. Overseas Student Health Cover: Student visa holders are required to have an OSHC.
Macquarie’s chosen provider of OSHC is Medibank. https://students.mq.edu.au/support/international/student-visa/overseas-student-health-cover
3. Accommodation: see an overview of on- and off-campus accommodation options. Contact all
providers directly for further support. https://students.mq.edu.au/uni-life/accommodation
4. Calendar of Dates: Find session start and end dates, enrolment deadlines, exam periods and
more for the academic year. https://www.mq.edu.au/study/admissions-and-entry/calendar
5. Course Handbook: Students must ensure that they have met the academic equivalent pre-
requisites at their home university for the units they want to study at Macquarie. See the Course
Handbook for unit overview, level, offerings, pre-requisites, learning outcomes, learning and
teaching activities. https://coursehandbook.mq.edu.au/
6. Unit Guide: information about staff contacts, learning outcomes, assessment tasks, delivery mode
and resources. https://unitguides.mq.edu.au/
7. Restricted Units List: Check the restricted units list list to see which units are not available to Study
Abroad and Exchange students. https://www.mq.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0006/1348719/Restricted-units-list-2026.pdf
8. Accessibility Services: Accessibility and disability support should be arranged at the time of
enrolment so that the University has adequate time to implement the required support. https://students.mq.edu.au/support/accessibility-disability
9. Support services: Macquarie University employs a robust support system including services for
student needs in academics, technology, health, wellbeing, counselling, and accessibility. https://students.mq.edu.au/support

* Cost of Living Information : Accommodation: private rental: $170-300 room/week or $400-800 house/week, unilodge: from $230/week, homestay: $300-345/week, food: $130-180 (food included for homestay), public transport: $30-60 or walk to university, utilities: $30+ (utilities included for unilidge and homestay), internet: $25+ (internet included for unilodge and homestay). 
* Southern Cross University (SCU) charges a one-off international student enrolment deposit which functions as a placement fee, and this deposit amount is specified on your offer letter; you can pay this deposit via the university's online payment portal. This fee is separate from tuition costs and Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC). 
* Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is mandatory health insurance for international students in Australia, covering expenses for medical services like doctors and public hospitals as a condition of their student visa. To apply, you must choose an approved OSHC provider (such as Bupa, Medibank, or Allianz Care), select a policy, purchase it, and submit the details with your visa application.

d02d8ef3-f3a4-479d-a1b4-873b46f9c5d4.value:
All incoming exchange students are required to show English language proficiency.

We accept the following standardized tests:
1. Bachelor
-TOEFL: TOEFL iBT: 75-85
-TOEFL pBT: 540
-IELTS or IELTS Online: 5.5-6.0 in academic module
-Cambridge English Business Vantage (BEC Vantage): Vantage with A/B in all skills
-Cambridge English Advanced (CAE): CAE with A/B in all skills
-PTE Academic: (PTE): 50
-Oxford Test of English: 111 in all skills

2. Master
-TOEFL: TOEFL iBT: 85-90
-TOEFL pBT: 560
-IELTS or IELTS Online: 6.5-7.0 in academic module
-Cambridge English Business Vantage (BEC Vantage): Higher with A/B in all skills
-Cambridge English Advanced (CAE): CAE or CPE with A/B in all skills
-PTE Academic: (PTE): 65
-Oxford Test of English: 120 in all skills

*Alternatively, we also offer an online English test free of charge. Details on our online test and the required scores are provided during the application period. 

*Students whose native language is English (including French-Canadians) or who are enrolled in a program fully taught in English at their home university are not required. No TOEFL ITP.

*Please note that the final list of courses open to incomings is only available during the course selection phase and that places are limited. Furthermore, it might not be possible to combine all courses due to overlapping timetables. Therefore, places in certain courses cannot be guaranteed in advance it is best if students can be quite flexible regarding their course topics.

All courses are taught in French.

- Accepted Language Tests: DELF, DALF
- Required Level Of French Language: 
  > For French Language courses (Inal’FLE): no minimum, full beginners accepted
  > For Language and Civilisation courses: minimum B1
  > Thematic and Disciplinary courses – minimum B1
  > For Professional Track courses: minimum C1 + B2 in English

Students can select courses from three different categories, according to their individual needs and French proficiency levels. 

Students who intend to take professional track courses (please see the “COURSES” section) might have to demonstrate a C1 level of French language and a B2 level of English language. All registrations to Professional Track courses will have to be approved by INALCO corresponding responsible.

*Please note that a French language test will be sent to all incoming students before their arrival at Inalco, regardless of the courses they decide to take. Its results will determine the group level to which the student will be registered at Inalco, regardless of other results from DELF/DALF exams.

554cd3c6-1c9c-4c8f-adee-ddb32e26eb25.name: Restrictions
554cd3c6-1c9c-4c8f-adee-ddb32e26eb25.value:
*Faculty of Sciences is not open to exchange students
*Courses in Film studies are restricted to students in Film studies at their home institution. Workshops cannot be attended.
*Courses in English studies are restricted to students enrolled in similar fields of studies at their home institution. 
*Courses from the Psychology Department are restricted to students enrolled in Psychology studies at their home institution. Workshops cannot be attended.
*Intercultural Studies and Applied Languages: courses in the second year of Master’s degree and in the third year of Bachelor apprenticeship degrees (L3 Pro) are not available to exchange students. 
*Sports courses: students may only register for one course per year to obtain credits. This does not apply to recreational sports courses (labeled “APSA”), which do not grant credits. 
*Students whose major in Kyung Hee is too far from their department of nomination at UPCité could not be accepted (for instance we will not accept a student in Engineering taking courses of History).
*Only students from the Grand Moulins Campus are allowed to take courses in other departments within the same campus

bea4403e-c18d-4922-903e-ba738acd5878.name: Accommodation
bea4403e-c18d-4922-903e-ba738acd5878.value:
Université Paris Cité can offer a few rooms in student residences in Paris (called CROUS).

The demand exceeds the number of rooms available. We cannot guarantee housing for all students.

Rooms in CROUS residences are equipped with a kitchenette, bathroom facilities and internet access.

While completing their application, students will have the option to request accommodation provided by UPCité. Students will receive an email notifying them if we were able to allocate them a CROUS room by the end of June for the 1st semester, and by December for the 2nd semester. A housing form will be sent to the selected students and will have to be submitted by the deadline to confirm housing.
Students placed in a CROUS residence must agree to pay until the last month of their contract, even if they decide to depart from the residence at an earlier date.
Please note that these residences are managed by the CROUS institution, and not by Université Paris Cité.
https://u-paris.fr/en/accomodation/

*The monthly costs for living in Germany typically include various expenses. Accommodation usually ranges between 250 and 350 euros per month. For meals, students can expect to pay around 3 to 4 euros per meal in the university canteen and an additional 80 to 130 euros for other food expenses. Statutory health insurance amounts to approximately 110 euros per month. Public transportation is generally free of charge, as it is covered by the semester ticket. Altogether, a monthly budget of 800 to 950 euros should be planned.

*The student dormitories are not administered by the University, but by the so-called “Studierendenwerk”, the Student Service Organization, which is not affiliated with the University. However, the University of Tübingen has a yearly quota of rooms that are reserved solely for exchange students. More info: https://uni-tuebingen.de/en/113870#c1818211.
*Please see for details of the dormitories the Overview of residence halls by the Studierendenwerk: https://www.my-stuwe.de/en/housing/halls-of-residence-tuebingen/

*We strongly recommend students to opt for student housing because of the difficult and expensive private housing market in Tübingen

*The Faculties of Humanities and Law will often let students from all faculties join their classes, with the understanding that students who are registered there will be prioritized if capacity issues arise.
*The Faculty of Medicine accepts applications only once per year. Please make sure to nominate students interested in studying at the Faculty of Medicine in the following academic year before the nomination deadline of 10 April. Students need to have completed at least three years of studies prior to exchange and provide proof of German
language proficiency level B1 CEFR.

B2 (iBT 72, IELTS 6.0, ITP 543)
Direct exchange students are exempt from a German language exam (for example, DSH or TestDaF), which is otherwise required for international degree-seeking students studying at a German university. However, we expect language skills equivalent to the B2 level of CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) for those wishing to study the humanities and social sciences and B1 for those wishing to study the natural sciences. A language certificate is not necessary because we expect our partner universities to ensure that students have the required language skills. Almost all subjects at undergraduate level are taught in German. Please note that subjects taught in English outside the Departments of English and North American Studies are very limited in number. Students must have an English language level of C1 to attend courses at the John F. Kennedy Institute for North American Studies. Availability may vary and cannot be guaranteed.

*Exchange students can take classes from both GLA and Faculty of Foreign Languages. Some classes are not open for students. Please refer to the course information.

Program 1: Japanese Language and Culture Program  (Bekka Program)
- The first and foremost aim of our program is to foster students’ language acquisition and ability to communicate with many types of Japanese speakers in a variety of interactive situations. Japanese speakers are invited to join the classes so that students can use their language skills they have acquired to communicate with them. 
- Students who meet the Japanese language proficiency requirements may enroll in undergraduate courses taught in Japanese. A wide range of subjects is available, including linguistics, interpreting and translation, area studies, communication, business, and international relations. These courses are taken alongside regular students, primarily Japanese nationals.
- Students who meet the English language proficiency requirements may also take undergraduate courses taught in English, together with regular students, primarily Japanese nationals.

Program 2: Undergraduate Courses in English
-In this program, students take the English-taught courses from the faculty of Foreign Languages or the faculty of Global Liberal Arts. Students can choose courses such as the Japan studies, U.S., British, and Oceania studies or linguistics. Especially, KUIS is very rich in the Japan studies, and students can deepen the knowledge.
-There are not any requirements about the Japanese language, but, students who have never studied Japanese have to take the Japanese for Daily Living course (two class hours per a week) and students who have studied Japanese ever can take up to 2 elective courses of Ryugakusei Bekka.

* See https://www.kandagaigo.ac.jp/kuis/english/students/bekka/ 
'Program Details' (JLCP Courses)
* Most of exchange students select classes form Bekka classes. Please refer to our website for more information.https://sites.google.com/kuis.ac.jp/intlstu/home-eng/en-exchange/en-exoutline?authuser=0

d02d8ef3-f3a4-479d-a1b4-873b46f9c5d4.name: Language Requirements
d02d8ef3-f3a4-479d-a1b4-873b46f9c5d4.value:
*Exchange students whose Japanese language ability is sufficiently high as proven on the Japanese language placement tests can enroll in classes provided by each faculty.
Students can learn a wide variety of subjects from general cultural subjects to specialist ones through these courses, held in the 13 faculties of Kansai University. These are studied in Japanese and students can expect an improvement in their level of Japanese proficiency as well as learning at a higher level of specialty.
The following is used as a guideline for the level of Japanese proficiency required to enroll in undergraduate courses.
・JLPT (Japanese Language Proficiency Test) N2 or higher
・J.TEST (Test of Practical Japanese) Level C or higher
・CEFR B2 or higher

* Regarding the language proficiency, students must have either Japanese or English ability. If they do not have Japanese ability, they need to have as much level of English ability shown below. They can take KUGF curriculum which is mainly taught in English.
・GTEC 260 ～ ・TOEFL ITP 505 ～ ・TOEFL iBT 60 ～ ・TOEIC 580 ～ ・IELTS 5.0 ・CEFR B1

d40e31b3-28c7-4beb-8ea0-b5de63a4fe38.name: Note
d40e31b3-28c7-4beb-8ea0-b5de63a4fe38.value:
【GTN】Starting from the 2026 academic year, our university has decided to introduce the "GTN assistants" for the purpose of enhancing the safety and well-being of international students. All international students will be required to enroll in this service.
Through this service, students can access lifestyle consultations and basic medical interpretation via 24-hour chat or phone support. It also provides useful daily life information, emergency disaster updates, and earthquake alerts.Please note that the cost of this service will be borne by the students themselves. For more details, please refer to the flyer. https://www.kansai-u.ac.jp/Kokusai/ES/GTNen.pdf
【National Health Insurance】
If students gets sick or injured during your stay in Japan, National Health Insurance makes it possible to receive medical treatment with only a part payment of the medical expenses (partial obligation). In principle, you can receive medical treatment with a payment of just 30% of the total medical care expenses. Exchange students are obligated to buy the National Health Insurance （13,000JPY to 14,000JPY per semester）
【Other costs】https://www.kansai-u.ac.jp/Kokusai/ES/expenses.pdf

From the Fall in 2024 onward, admission guideline for exchange program will be changed partially. Therefore please be noted information below.

1. For applicants for exchange program who have language proficiency of JLPT N2 level or higher and are required to take regular undergraduate courses at Fukuoka Univ. which are related to their major field of study. The admission shall be standardized in April, at the timing of undergraduate course programs' opening anew for the academic year's starting. 2. For applicants for exchange program whose language proficiency are JLPT N3 or N4 level and are required to take Japanese Language and Culture Course. The admission shall be standardized in September at the timing of Japanese Language and Culture Course's opening anew. Since the Course's curriculum is designed on a year-round teaching, the exchange students shall be accepted for the period from September to August of the next year (one year) or from September to January of the next year (Fall semester only). The application guideline will be sent in December of the previous year.

Cost of medical assistance service for international students to be joined after arriving in Japan: 2,900 yen per year.
*All students are required to enter Japan on the designated entry date and use the pick-up service.
*Should any student fall into one of the following categories, we may need to consult with you about the possibility of canceling their study abroad program;
   1) Students who require ongoing medical treatment in Japan but are unable to attend appointments independently due to their health condition or Japanese language limitations
   2) Students who may pose a risk of harm to themselves or others
We sincerely ask for your understanding of this matter.
* All applicants must submit a “Health Certificate” stating that they are “fit to study abroad,” signed by a physician who is thoroughly familiar with their health condition. Depending on the contents of the medical certificate, our university maybe unable to accept the applicant. Should health issues arise during the study abroad period, or should our university instruct the students to discontinue their studies or return home urgently, we request that the students’ home university and guardians assume responsibility for providing support to the student.

MODULE CATALOGUES: http://modules.xjtlu.edu.cn/dept
Students normally study 10-25 credits each semester. 25 credits is full study load of a degree student in XJTLU

Erasmus School of History, Culture and Communication(ESHCC) 혹은 Erasmus University College(EUC)로 신청할 수 있으며, 각각 지원자격 및 수강가능 과목범위가 다를 수 있으니 반드시 파견교 웹사이트 및 팩트시트를 통해 확인하시기 바랍니다. 
* ESHCC : https://www.eur.nl/en/eshcc/education/incoming-exchange/courses-and-study-information/eshcc-courses
• The fulltime (and maximum) ECTS allowed during the exchange programme is 30 ECTS per semester (15 OR 17.5 ECTS per term). If your course registrations exceed the maximum workload per Term (which is 15 OR 17.5 ECTS), you will be randomly unenrolled from courses. 
• The minimum amount of ECTS you are required to take per term is 5 ECTS. 
• Courses not mentioned in the course offer list are NOT open to exchange students.
• ESHCC exchange students should follow at least 50% of their total number of courses within their host department (i.e. Arts & Culture Studies, History, or Communication & Media). You also have access to designated courses in other academic fields/Faculties at Erasmus University Rotterdam based on schedule availability and subject to being approved by the respective programme directors.

bea4403e-c18d-4922-903e-ba738acd5878.value:
Leiden University does not have its own dormitories; instead, students live in accommodation offered by external housing agencies and private landlords throughout Leiden and The Hague.
Each year, the university reserves a limited number of rooms through DUWO for new international students, with priority given to short -term students, such as exchange students and one -year master’s students . Although housing cannot be guaranteed, students may apply for university housing as soon as they submit their
application for admission —there is no need to wait for an admission decision

** Applicants MUST check all the information carefully, especially about study programmes and course registration.

*Course of Business might be limited in numbers

This may be demonstrated by, for example, an international English test (such as IELTS or TOEFL), a certificate from the coordinator at your home university, or a transcript of records showing previous studies with English as the language of instruction. The recommended English requirements for exchange students are TOEFL iBT 72 or above, IELTS 6.0 and TOEFL ITP 543. d02d8ef3-f3a4-479d-a1b4-873b46f9c5d4.name: Language Requirements
d02d8ef3-f3a4-479d-a1b4-873b46f9c5d4.value:
If English is not your first language, you must submit official results from an English test you have taken within the past two years from your application submission date.  
For exchange application, applicants must submit official test results in PDF format through the UNM exchange application website (obtain the website from your home institution). Test scores CANNOT be directly sent from the test center to the University of New Mexico.  
The tests we accept, and the minimum scores we require on each, are:  
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) – Undergraduate: 68 on the Internet-Based Test (IBT) 
*Unofficial (ITP) scores are not accepted.  TOEFL iBT MyBest Scores and TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition are now accepted after Spring 2021 application.  
International English Language Testing System (IELTS) – Undergraduate: 6.0 
IELTS Indicator scores are not accepted. 
NOTE: You are exempt from submitting English test scores if you meet one or both of the following conditions 1) You received a high school diploma from an accredited, English-speaking institution in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, or New Zealand. 2) You have attended a university where English is the medium of instruction for at least one year of full-time study at the time of your application.

*Course Approval & Denial :  After admission, students will be asked to complete the ASP&E Course Request Form. Through this form, students will be asked to select up to 10 courses of interest. These courses will be reviewed by the corresponding MSU college. Decisions about enrollment eligibility will be made based on the students transcripts and academic background, along with any supporting coursework the student provides to accompany the form. (https://americansemester.isp.msu.edu/interested-students/about-academics/exchange-course-availability/ )
*MSU requires that all students enrolling in classes be vaccinated and boosted (3 doses) against COVID-19
with a World Health Organization approved vaccine. Vaccination must be completed prior to course
enrollment. Students will be asked to verify their vaccination status prior to enrolling in classes.
*Insurance : Tuition does not include mandatory student health insurance. This cost ranges from semester to semester; for reference, the average cost is typically between $1,400-$1,800 per semester depending on semester duration. Students must be prepared to take this insurance, as students are not permitted to opt out of MSU’s health insurance policy, even if the home university or government supplies insurance.
*Housing Office now requires a $50 non-refundable application fee and a $175 advanced housing payment (which is applied to the contract cost). These are not yet reflected in the cost section of the factsheet but should be accounted for when financial planning.
